outcomes.text: Name the movements at the shoulder, elbow, wrist, hip, knee and ankle, and the muscles that produce them.
Describe the frontal, transverse and sagittal planes of movement.
Explain the agonist, antagonist and fixator roles of muscles.
Distinguish isotonic (concentric, eccentric) and isometric contractions.
Analyse a movement by joint type, movement produced, muscles involved and contraction type.
Explain motor units and nervous stimulation: motor neuron, action potential, neurotransmitter and the all-or-none law.
Describe slow oxidative, fast oxidative glycolytic and fast glycolytic fibres and their recruitment at different intensities and in recovery.
Explain the relationship between heart rate, stroke volume and cardiac output, resting values and how to calculate them.
Explain the cardiac cycle (diastole, systole) and the heart's conduction system.
Describe the effects of different intensities and recovery on heart rate, stroke volume and cardiac output.
Explain redistribution of cardiac output: the vascular shunt, vasomotor centre, arterioles and pre-capillary sphincters.
Explain venous return mechanisms during exercise and recovery.
Explain neural, hormonal and intrinsic regulation of heart rate.
Explain breathing frequency, tidal volume and minute ventilation at rest and how to calculate them.
Explain the mechanics of breathing at rest: diaphragm and external intercostals.
Describe the effects of exercise intensity and recovery on breathing frequency, tidal volume and minute ventilation.
Explain the extra muscles in exercise breathing: sternocleidomastoid and pectoralis minor for inspiration, internal intercostals and rectus abdominis for expiration.
Explain neural and chemical control of breathing.
Explain gas exchange at alveoli and muscles: pressure gradients and oxyhaemoglobin dissociation.
Explain the function and importance of carbohydrates, proteins, fats, minerals, vitamins, fibre and water in a balanced diet.
Explain energy intake, expenditure and balance in performance.
Evaluate pharmacological aids: anabolic steroids, EPO and HGH.
Evaluate physiological aids: blood doping, intermittent hypoxic training and cooling aids.
Evaluate nutritional aids: meal amount, composition and timing, hydration, carbohydrate loading, creatine, caffeine, bicarbonate and nitrate.
Explain aerobic capacity and VO2max and what affects it.
Describe methods of evaluating aerobic capacity: gas analysis, multi-stage fitness test, Queen's College step test and Cooper 12 minute run.
Explain continuous and HIIT training, using target heart rates as an intensity guide.
Explain the cardiovascular, respiratory, muscular and metabolic adaptations from aerobic training and sports where aerobic capacity is key.
Distinguish the types of strength and the factors affecting strength.
Describe methods of evaluating strength: dynamometer, 1RM, press-up or sit-up and vertical jump tests.
Explain strength training methods: repetitions, sets, resistance, multi-gym, weights, plyometrics and circuits.
Explain adaptations from strength training and sports where strength is key.
Distinguish types of flexibility and factors affecting it.
Describe methods of evaluating flexibility: sit and reach test and goniometer.
Explain passive, PNF, static, dynamic, ballistic and isometric stretching.
Explain adaptations from flexibility training and sports where flexibility is key.
Explain macrocycles, mesocycles and microcycles, and preparatory, competitive and transition phases and tapering.
Plan personal health and fitness programmes for aerobic, strength and flexibility training.
Explain the effect of training on lifestyle diseases: CHD, stroke, atherosclerosis, heart attack, asthma and COPD.
Define and apply Newton's first, second and third laws.
Explain net force, balanced and unbalanced forces, weight, reaction, friction and air resistance.
Draw free body diagrams and calculate force, momentum, acceleration and weight.
Explain centre of mass, what affects it and its relationship with stability.
Describe the components of 1st, 2nd and 3rd class levers and the mechanical advantage of a 2nd class lever.
Explain how limb kinematics, force plates and wind tunnels optimise performance.
Justify the placement of skills on continua: difficulty, environment, pacing, muscular involvement, continuity and organisation.
Explain part, whole, whole-part-whole, progressive, massed, distributed, fixed and varied practice.
Explain positive, negative, proactive, retroactive and bilateral transfer and how to optimise or limit it.
Explain operant conditioning, cognitive theory and Bandura's observational learning.
Describe the cognitive, associative and autonomous stages of learning.
Compare verbal, visual, manual and mechanical guidance.
Compare intrinsic, extrinsic, positive, negative feedback, knowledge of performance and knowledge of results.
Define personality and explain trait, social learning and interactionist theories.
Define attitude, its formation and components, and methods of attitude change.
Define intrinsic and extrinsic motivation and their uses and effects.
Explain arousal and drive theory, inverted U theory and catastrophe theory.
Explain state and trait anxiety, somatic and cognitive responses and the zone of optimal functioning.
Explain instinct, social learning, frustration-aggression and aggressive cue theories of aggression.
Explain social facilitation and inhibition, the effect of an audience, evaluative apprehension and strategies to minimise inhibition.
Define a group and explain Tuckman's stages: forming, storming, norming, performing.
Explain Steiner's model of group effectiveness.
Explain the Ringelmann effect and social loafing.
Explain the importance of goal setting for focus, persistence, confidence, arousal control and monitoring.
Apply the SMART principle.

units.title: H555/03 Socio-cultural issues in physical activity and sport

subtopics.title: Sport in pre-industrial and industrial Britain

outcomes.text: Explain how social class, gender, law and order, literacy, time, money and transport shaped sport and pastimes in pre-industrial Britain.
Explain how class, amateurism and professionalism, women's status, work conditions, money and railways shaped sport in post-1850 industrial Britain.
Explain the influence of public schools: organising sport, promoting ethics, the cult of athleticism and exporting games.
Explain how class, amateurism and professionalism, gender, law and order, education, time, money and transport shaped 20th century sport.
Explain how the same factors shape 21st century sport.
Explain the globalisation of sport: media coverage, freedom of movement for performers and greater exposure.
Describe the background and aims of the modern Olympic Games (1896).
Explain political exploitation: Berlin 1936, Mexico City 1968, Munich 1972, Moscow 1980 and Los Angeles 1984.
Evaluate the sporting, social, economic and political impacts of hosting global events such as the Olympics or World Cup.
Explain ATP as energy currency and the coupled reactions of ATP breakdown and resynthesis.
Describe the ATP-PC, glycolytic and aerobic systems: reaction type, fuel, site, enzyme, ATP yield, stages and by-products.
Explain the energy continuum and which system predominates at different intensities and durations.
Interpret figures showing the energy systems' contributions to exercise.
Explain the interplay of energy systems in intermittent exercise and what affects it.
Explain EPOC and its fast components: replenishing oxygen stores and resynthesising ATP and PC.
Explain EPOC's slow components: elevated circulation, ventilation and temperature, and lactate removal.
Explain how exercise intensity affects EPOC and the implications for planning sessions.

subtopics.title: Exercise at altitude and in the heat

outcomes.text: Explain the effect of altitude on cardiovascular and respiratory systems, and acclimatisation.
Explain the effect of heat on cardiovascular and respiratory systems: temperature regulation and cardiovascular drift.
Distinguish acute and chronic hard and soft tissue injuries, and concussion.
Explain intrinsic and extrinsic risk factors for injury.
Discuss the debate on effective warm up and cool down.
Assess sporting injuries using SALTAPS.
Apply PRICE to acute soft tissue injuries and the Recognise and Remove approach to concussion.
Explain treatment of fractures, joint injuries and muscle damage with stretching, massage, heat and cold, drugs, physiotherapy and surgery.
Define linear motion and how a direct force through the centre of mass creates it.
Calculate distance, displacement, speed, velocity and acceleration with units.
Plot and interpret distance/time, speed/time and velocity/time graphs.
Define angular motion and how an eccentric force creates it about the longitudinal, frontal and transverse axes.
Calculate moment of inertia, angular velocity and angular momentum and know what affects moment of inertia.
Explain conservation of angular momentum in flight and interpret related graphs.
Explain how velocity, cross-sectional area, streamlining and surface affect air resistance and drag.
Explain how release height, speed and angle affect projectile distance.
Draw force diagrams for projectiles and explain parabolic and non-parabolic flight paths.
Apply Bernoulli's principle to lift, downward force and the Magnus effect of spin in sport.
Explain the Atkinson and Shiffrin multi-store model and selective attention.
Explain Craik and Lockhart's levels of processing model.
Relate both models to learning and performing skills.
Explain Weiner's model: stability, locus of causality and controllability.
Explain learned helplessness and mastery orientation.
Define sports confidence and self-efficacy and their impact on performance, participation and self-esteem.
Explain Vealey's model of sports confidence.
Explain Bandura's four sources of self-efficacy.
Describe the characteristics of effective leaders and emergent versus prescribed leaders.
Compare autocratic, democratic and laissez-faire styles.
Explain trait, social learning and interactionist theories and Chelladurai's multi-dimensional model.
Define stress and explain its causes.
Apply cognitive techniques: self-talk, thought stopping, rational thinking, mental rehearsal, imagery, goal setting and mindfulness.
Apply somatic techniques: progressive muscular relaxation, biofeedback, centring and breathing control.

units.title: H555/03 Socio-cultural issues in physical activity and sport

topics.title: 3.2 Contemporary issues in physical activity and sport

outcomes.text: Distinguish legal supplements from illegal drugs and doping, and explain why elite performers dope.
Evaluate the consequences of doping for society, sport and performers, and strategies to stop it.
Explain causes of violence in sport, its implications and prevention strategies for players and spectators.
Explain gambling in sport: match fixing, bribery and illegal betting.
Explain factors driving commercialisation: public interest, media, professionalism, advertising and sponsorship.
Evaluate the impacts of commercialisation on society, sports, performers and spectators.
Compare media coverage of sport since the 1980s on terrestrial, satellite and pay-per-view TV, radio, press and internet.
Evaluate the effects of the media on sport and the 'golden triangle' of sport, media and sponsorship.

subtopics.title: Routes to sporting excellence in the UK

outcomes.text: Describe development routes from talent identification to elite performance.
Explain the roles of schools, clubs and universities in elite success.
Explain the role of UK Sport and National Institutes in high performance sport.
Explain strategies to address drop-out and failure rates in elite development.
Evaluate how technology has affected elite sport: access, facilities, equipment, monitoring and safety.
Evaluate how technology has increased or limited general participation.
Evaluate how technology has increased or decreased fair outcomes, such as timing, officials, foul play and doping detection.
Evaluate how technology has increased or reduced entertainment, such as replays, camera angles and delays.
